## Diverging Signals

**The sharpest tension this run is between a news feed that has turned and a price snapshot that cannot respond.** The daemon moved CLEAR → CAUTION at shock 13.5 on tariff headlines, timestamped this morning (2026-08-31T09:00Z). Every equity index level and every TQQQ field available to me is from the **2026-08-27 close** — before the two sessions in which those headlines circulated. So I can see the news impulse and I cannot see the market's answer to it. Anyone reading this report should treat the equity table as describing the market *before* the tariff flow, not after.

**Second: the volatility complex is now split across dates and partially blind.** VIX rose +5.31% to 15.28 on 2026-08-31 — the fresh print, and it moved *up*. VXN fell −5.51% to 20.24 on 2026-08-27 — the stale print, and it moved *down*. These are two different days pointing opposite ways, and I cannot reconcile them into a single vol read. Worse, the **VIX/VIX3M term ratio is unavailable**, so the one measure that would tell me whether near-dated risk is being repriced above longer-dated risk — the exact thing a fresh tariff impulse would show up in — is the measure I have lost. VVIX at 82.90 and MOVE at 69.86 still say calm, but they are also 2026-08-27 stamps.

**Third, and the one that matters most for premium selling: IV/HV has gone dark at exactly the wrong moment.** It printed 1.02, then 0.94 — moving steadily toward the 0.85 level I named as the hostile threshold, meaning options were paying less than TQQQ's actual movement. There is no ATM IV and no HV20 this run, so the series simply stops. **A blind trigger is not a cleared trigger.** The last known direction was deteriorating, and the honest position is that the premium environment was below parity two sessions ago and is now unknown — not that it recovered.

**Fourth: SKEW 144.05 against the rest of Lens 2**, unchanged from last read and now more interesting. VVIX and MOVE say no one is worried. SKEW says someone is still paying up for crash protection. With a tariff impulse arriving after those prints were taken, the residual tail bid is the dissenting voice that looks most prescient rather than least.

**Fifth: NDX remains the weakest major index while having led the tape.** NDX at −4.3% below its 52-week high is nearly 4× SPX's −1.1% gap, yet it led at +1.43% on 2026-08-27. A single-name reaction (NVDA) lifting the index it dominates is not broad participation recovering. Breadth would settle this, and breadth is dark for the third read running.

## TQQQ Read

- **Momentum:** **RSI(14) at 47.0 is neutral** — dead mid-range, unchanged from last read because the underlying stamp has not advanced. No overbought stretch to fade, no oversold spring to lean on. This is the least informative momentum state for a put-seller: neither the thin premium of an extended rally nor the fat premium and mean-reversion tailwind of a washed-out low. The **3 consecutive green days** stand alongside it — a short up-streak into a neutral RSI, the last of those days a +4.02% NVDA-reaction move. That was a bounce that had not yet proven itself a trend as of 2026-08-27, and I have no data covering whether it has since.

- **Market structure: SIDEWAYS — fully measured, both legs.** **DOWNTURN fails on both conditions:** the $73.30 close is **5.9% below** the 4-week high of $77.90, nowhere near the >20% required, and VXN 19.92 is well below the ≥25 threshold. **RALLY fails too:** the close is **17.5% above** the 4-week low of $62.39 (73.30 / 62.39 − 1), short of the >30% required. Neither branch triggers, so **SIDEWAYS**. Note this is computed from the close rather than a live spot; the margins on both tests are wide enough (5.9% vs 20%, 17.5% vs 30%) that two sessions of ordinary movement could not flip the classification — a genuine gap would be needed.

- **Trend:** **Above both moving averages on the last available print.** The close is **+20.5% above the 200DMA (~$60.83)** — an intact longer-term uptrend with a wide cushion, and the single most robust bullish fact in the instrument analysis. Against the **50DMA at $72.29**, the close sits +1.40% above. The honest caveat: last read's live spot was *below* that line, so price has been oscillating around the 50DMA, and with no live quote this run I cannot say where it stands today. Treat the 50DMA as unresolved rather than as support that is holding.

- **Volatility & premium environment: UNKNOWN — and the not-knowing is itself the finding.** For two consecutive reads I could state this precisely: ATM IV 51.9% vs HV20 51.0% gave IV/HV 1.02, then 51.0% vs 54.6% gave 0.94 — a deteriorating series showing options priced at roughly 94 cents per dollar of actual movement, i.e. **no variance risk premium at all, slightly negative**. This run there is no ATM IV and no HV20, so the series stops. What I can still say: **absolute** premium is low — VXN 19.92 is 41% below its 52-week high, and although the term structure is unavailable, VVIX 82.90 and MOVE 69.86 (both 2026-08-27) were subdued. What I cannot say is whether the **relative** compensation recovered, held, or deteriorated further. Given the last known reading was below parity and falling, and given a tariff news impulse has since arrived, the reasonable working assumption is that it has not improved — but that is an inference, not a measurement, and I am flagging it as one.

- **Put-selling context: CAUTIOUS.** The macro backdrop remains genuinely supportive and is why the total holds at +2: credit spreads are tight (HY OAS 2.63%, IG 0.79%), the yield curve is normally sloped (2s10s +0.39%), the commodity complex is soft without credit confirming stress, and the 200DMA sits 17.0% below the last close. Those are real supports. Against them, four things argue for restraint, and they bear on premium selling specifically rather than on market direction. First, **the premium read is blind** — IV/HV printed 1.02 then 0.94 and is now unavailable; a seller cannot see today whether they are being paid above or below what the underlying actually moves, and the last known answer was *below*. Second, **the news feed has turned CAUTION at shock 13.5 on tariff headlines**, a category weighted 2× precisely because it gaps indices without warning, and **the entire equity snapshot predates that flow**. Third, **NFP lands on 2026-09-04, inside the 5-day window**, into a 10Y sitting 1.6% below its 52-week high. Fourth, **price is unresolved against its 50DMA** and 3 of 7 lenses remain dark. A structurally sound tape whose compensation cannot currently be measured, with a fresh policy-headline impulse the price data has not yet absorbed. Context only — no strikes, expiries, sizes, or trade calls.
